title: Exact isomorphism transport through integral and field coefficient stages
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, not assumed separated, and let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, not necessarily over $k$, with inverse $\bar g$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, write $\mathcal O_E$ for its valuation ring, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the completed integral constructible category $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E(W)[1/\varpi_E]=D^b_c(W,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the common-stage category $D^b_c(W,\Omega)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], for $W=X,Y$. Write $P_{g,E}=Lg_E^*$ for the prescribed completed pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Normalize its comparison $\lambda^g:P_{g,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}$ as in [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback, lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension], where the inverse image on modules is through the canonical completed coefficient isomorphism of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image].

The functors $P_{g,E}$ and $P_{\bar g,E}$ are exact inverse equivalences on these integral categories. On completed module sheaves the transport is the exact inverse-image equivalence, with coefficient isomorphism
$$g^{-1}\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y\simeq\varprojlim_ng^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y\simeq\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X.$$
The inverse-composition comparison on $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$ is the specified natural isomorphism
$$\epsilon^E_K=\bigl(\bar g^{-1}g^{-1}K\simeq K\bigr)\circ\bar g^{-1}(\lambda^g_K)\circ\lambda^{\bar g}_{P_{g,E}K}:P_{\bar g,E}P_{g,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,$$
and the opposite composite has the same formula with $g,\bar g$ exchanged. The realization by termwise inverse image preserves shifts and distinguished triangles.

At the rational stage the same object formulas and the rule $u\otimes c\mapsto P_{g,E}(u)\otimes c$, extended additively, give exact inverse equivalences; their inverse comparisons are the images of $\epsilon^E$ and its opposite. They are natural for all localized morphisms, including those not represented by a single integral morphism.

For $E\subset L$ write $T_W=-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] and $\alpha^g:T_XP_{g,E}\simeq P_{g,L}T_Y$ for the canonical comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with the whole-system normalization of [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension]. The inverse comparisons obey
$$\epsilon^L_{T_YK}\circ P_{\bar g,L}(\alpha^g_K)\circ\alpha^{\bar g}_{P_{g,E}K}=T_Y(\epsilon^E_K),$$
and the analogous equation with $g,\bar g$ exchanged. On common-stage objects put $P_g(E,K)=(E,P_{g,E}K)$; on an arrow represented by $u:K\otimes_E L\to K'\otimes_{E'}L$ use
$$[L,(\alpha^g_{E',L})^{-1}P_{g,L}(u)\alpha^g_{E,L}].$$
Here the $\alpha$ in this formula are rationalized. This is independent of representatives and common fields and defines an exact equivalence with inverse $P_{\bar g}$. Its natural inverse-composition comparison at $(E,K)$ is $[E,\epsilon^E_K]$, and likewise for the opposite composite. Thus these exactness and inverse identities use the actual common-stage arrows and triangles, without adjoining retracts or assuming separatedness.

For the application to inv g, construct its opposite normalized family directly at inv (inv g), using the same finite-stage and scalar-localization theorems; this avoids transporting record data through a dependent inverse-instance equality. This supplies the exact additive common-stage equivalences, own-stage epsilon formulas and shift comparisons required in the original conclusion.
